Use this before you add tags, so that you reuse the names that exist. It keeps your tags consistent.

## CLI

### gournal tags

List every tag that you use, with the number of entries for each tag.

```text
gournal tags
```

## MCP tool

### list_tags

List every tag in use, with the number of entries for each tag. Call this before you add tags, to reuse existing ones.

#### Input

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `project` | `string` | no | Count tags of this project only. |

#### Output

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `tags` | `object[]` | yes | Tags, most used first. |
| `tags.tag` | `string` | yes | Tag name. |
| `tags.count` | `number` | yes | Number of entries with this tag. |

## Examples

### CLI

List every tag with its number of entries. The most used tags come first.

```console
$ gournal tags
#invoices  2
#ui  2
#a11y  1
#bugfix  1
#testing  1
#webhooks  1
```

### MCP

List the tags of one project before you add an entry. Reuse these names.

```json
{
  "project": "billing-api"
}
```

The structured result:

```json
{
  "tags": [
    { "tag": "invoices", "count": 2 },
    { "tag": "bugfix", "count": 1 },
    { "tag": "docs", "count": 1 },
    { "tag": "testing", "count": 1 },
    { "tag": "webhooks", "count": 1 }
  ]
}
```

The text result holds the `tags` list as JSON.
